item.title: Florida executes man who killed deputy after fighting for gun
item.description: Florida carried out its 18th execution this year under Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis' aggressive use of the death penalty.

item.title: Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's access to SpaceX network, sources say
item.description: A decision by Elon Musk led to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's satellite communications network, people familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Iran touts closest ever ties with Russia, contradicting Trump
item.description: Iran says its ties with Russia are stronger than ever after a visit by Putin's top envoy, challenging Trump's assertion that Moscow isn't helping Iran in the war.

item.title: The AI doom scenario you've never heard of may be hardest to stop
item.description: The time to prepare for "gradual disempowerment" is now, according to researchers. One calls it "a civilization-scale problem."

item.title: The often neglected AI doom scenario that poses a different kind of threat to humanity
item.description: Some researchers warn that as artificial intelligence agents take on more and more tasks, humans could end up giving up their critical thinking skills in a scenario they call "gradual disempowerment." Jay Chooi, co-founder and CEO of Robocurve, a company that tracks AI-driven robots, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: The risks of trusting personal AI agents with your money, data
item.description: With personal AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots hitting the market, experts are warning of the risks associated with giving these chatbots access to your data and money. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Democratic presidential contenders to gather for post-midterm summit in Denver
item.description: Potential 2028 Democratic presidential contenders are set to gather in Denver for a post-midterm summit. CBS News political director Fin Gómez reports.

item.title: Elon Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's use of SpaceX satellite network, sources say
item.description: Elon Musk chose to limit Ukraine's access to SpaceX's satellite service, affecting drone operations, sources say.

item.title: What to know about Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis
item.description: Jalen Hurts' agent and the Eagles said in a statement Monday his "prognosis is very good, and we anticipate a full recovery."

item.title: Trump says U.S. has gotten "nothing" from Ukraine
item.description: President Trump on Tuesday said the U.S. has "given a lot" to Ukraine and gotten "nothing" in return amid Russia's ongoing war with the country. CBS News' Aaron MacLean has more.

item.title: Cornell responds to Jane Doe letter saying she felt disbelieved
item.description: Cornell has denied claims made in a letter from a former student, known as Jane Doe, about a remark by the school's president.

item.title: Doctor explains how a misdiagnosis of multiple sclerosis happens amid Christina Applegate news
item.description: Actress Christina Applegate revealed on her podcast Tuesday that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis. CBS News' medical correspondent Dr. Cèline Gounder explains what could have happened.

item.title: LeBron James making debut with 76ers as NBA season kicks off
item.description: LeBron James is making his regular-season debut with the 76ers on Tuesday, as the 2026-2027 NBA season gets underway. Jason Jones, staff writer at The Athletic, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Eighth graders rally around new classmate to help her dazzle at big Halloween party
item.description: After one student's family moved to Florida, she felt she had to really wow the other kids at her new neighborhood's Halloween party. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Prince Harry says he hopes to reconcile with royal family
item.description: Prince Harry and his family returned to live in the U.K. six years after a very public split from the royals, including his father, King Charles. Harry is now hoping for a very public reconciliation to match. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Beloved Washington, D.C., bookstore Kramers celebrates 50 years in business
item.description: Washington, D.C., institution Kramers is celebrating its 50th anniversary. Several notable names have patronized the Dupont Circle bookstore over the years, from former President Barack Obama to Andy Warhol. Its owner, Steve Salis, joins "The Takeout" to unpack the store's storied past.

item.title: Italy agrees to send Texas man accused of killing pregnant wife back to U.S.
item.description: A Texas man who was accused of killing his pregnant wife two years ago fled to Italy. Officials there have agreed to send him back to the U.S. to face charges on the condition that he faces a lesser charge, not capital murder. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Fear, outrage in New Jersey after ICE questions young person outside high school
item.description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security said Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents arrested nine undocumented migrants, all with criminal records, near a high school in northern New Jersey. But officials there said the agents are also questioning nearby residents, stirring fear in the community. Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Jay Feely, Arizona Republican House candidate and former NFL kicker, talks campaign
item.description: Former NFL kicker Jay Feely is seeking a House seat in Arizona as a Republican. Feely, who was also a former analyst for CBS Sports, joins "The Takeout" to discuss his campaign.

item.title: Democrats gain seats in new Sabato's Crystal Ball ratings
item.description: Sabato's Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia changed its ratings in 28 House races on Tuesday, with Democrats now favored in more than 220 seats. Sabato's Crystal Ball managing editor Kyle Kondik and CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto join to discuss.

item.title: Trump looks to boost Republicans in North Carolina two weeks out from Election Day
item.description: President Trump is rallying in North Carolina on Tuesday as Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley trails Democrat Roy Cooper in the polls. CBS News chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Trump criss-crosses U.S. for Republican candidates
item.description: With two weeks until election day and control of Congress on the line, President Trump says he plans to spend more than $400 million on the races. Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Christina Applegate reveals she was misdiagnosed with MS
item.description: Christina Applegate said on her MeSsy podcast that her doctor recently revealed she did not have multiple sclerosis.

item.title: Christina Applegate says new technology revealed her MS misdiagnosis
item.description: Christina Applegate, who has been waging a public battle with the autoimmune disease multiple sclerosis, announced Tuesday that she discovered she does not, in fact, have MS. She is now one of an estimated 25 million Americans living with a rare or undiagnosed illness. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: American Airlines brake issue prompts emergency landing
item.description: An American Airlines jet reported a brake problem and then blew out a tire while making an emergency landing in Chicago Tuesday. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Cornell faculty member alleges "silencing of Jane Doe's voice"
item.description: Some Cornell faculty members say they were not shown a letter apparently from Jane Doe, who said she "felt unsupported and disbelieved" by university president Michael Kotlikoff.

item.title: Early voting underway in Florida as Clinton campaigns for Jolly
item.description: More than a million people have already voted in Florida as Former President Bill Clinton makes a campaign stop in the state to support Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly. CBS News' Cristian Benavides has more.

item.title: Trump pushes Zelenskyy to end war with Russia as fuel prices rise with midterms looming
item.description: President Trump is claiming Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has the power to end the country's war with Russia as Americans feel the impact of rising fuel prices with midterms just a few weeks away. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata and Natalie Brand report.

item.title: Ohio race takes ugly turn with ad featuring Amy Acton's mother
item.description: Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar in a new GOP ad. Acton's brother says the ad marks a "despicable low" and says their stepfather sexually abused Acton when she was a child.

item.title: 10/20: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: 14 days until midterm contests; President Trump looks to boost Republicans in North Carolina elections.
